players.note:
We should at least consider the possibility that Omar Cooper Jr. is a budding star.

Cooper has topped 100 yards and scored a touchdown in each of his first two games back from the high-ankle sprain he sustained in Week 1. The former Indiana University star had 6-103-1 on seven targets against the Patriots in Week 6, then had 5-115-1 on five targets against the Dolphins in Week 7.

Although he's only seen 13 NFL targets, Cooper is averaging an outrageous 19.1 yards per target.

Garrett Wilson has been the Jets' No. 1 receiver early in the season, and we shouldn't expect Cooper to overtake Wilson as the team target leader. But it's reasonable to think that Cooper, the 30th overall pick in this year's draft, can overtake Adonai Mitchell as the Jets' No. 2 receiver.

In fact, it may have already happened.

Cooper played 38 snaps and ran 23 routes on Sunday. Mitchell played 26 snaps and ran 18 routes. Mitchell was returning from a finger injury that had kept him out of action since Week 2, so it's possible the Jets were working him back into things slowly. But Cooper played ahead of Mitchell in two-receiver sets on Sunday, and there's a good chance it will remain that way.

Fantasy managers needing to patch a hole at wide receiver should make a run at Cooper in leagues where he's available in hopes that we're seeing the start of something big.

When we last saw the Jaguars before their Week 7 bye, Jakobi Meyers had 5-83-0 against the Texans on a season-high 10 targets.

For the season, Meyers has 20-285-2 on 28 targets. He was WR36 in half-point PPR fantasy scoring through the first six weeks of the season. Meyers is averaging a solid 10.2 yards per target and 1.85 yards per route run.

Although Meyers has a modest 15.2% target share, that percentage could increase in the coming weeks, with Brian Thomas Jr. no longer drawing a significant number of targets and rumored to be a trade candidate.

Meyers is averaging 2.06 yards per route run and 0.28 targets per route run against man coverage this season, and in Week 8 he faces a Colts defense that's playing man coverage at the sixth-highest rate in the league, per Fantasy Points Data.

Jonah Coleman is going to command some serious attention on waivers this week.

You might recall the waiver enthusiasm for Coleman in Week 3, when it seemed as if JK Dobbins and RJ Harvey were both in danger of missing time with hamstring issues. There were some zesty FAAB bids for Coleman that week. It turned out that Dobbins and Harvey were fine — neither missed a game — but Coleman had a high-ankle sprain that required a stay on injured reserve.

Well, Coleman made his return in Week 7, and it appears he's now Denver's No. 1 running back,

Coleman had 9-54-0 rushing and 2-15-0 receiving in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Cardinals. Dobbins had 6-23-1 rushing with no receptions. Harvey had 3-6-0 rushing and 2-54-1 receiving.

Coleman played 30 snaps on Sunday, while Harvey played 16 and Dobbins 14. Coleman ran 11 pass routes, Harvey eight, Dobbins two.

Broncos beat writer Zac Stevens quoted Broncos head coach Sean Payton as saying of Coleman after the game: "Got to get him more touches. Definitely." Payton also said Coleman provided "juice" and looked "really good," per Stevens.

Payton habitually used two- or three-man backfields during his long tenure as head coach of the Saints, and this Denver backfield could be a three-way affair. But for Coleman to immediately lead the Denver RBs in snaps in his first game back suggests that he will have the meatiest role going forward.

A fourth-round pick from the University of Washington, the 5-8, 220-pound Coleman has good vision and contact balance, and he's an able pass-catcher and pass blocker.

It's rare for plug-and-play running backs to be available on waivers, which is why Coleman is going to command a fortune in FAAB money this week. It's probably going to take $25 for you to have any chance of getting Coleman, and it might require $50 or more to land him with the winning bid.

With Terry McLaurin out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, rookie Antonio Williams figures to play an expanded role in the Commanders' passing attack going forward. So far this season, Williams has 18-205-1 on 26 targets.

A third-round pick out of Clemson, Williams is a terrific athlete who ran a 4.41 and had a 39 1/2-inch vertical jump at the NFL Scouting Combine. Williams returned kicks in college and is dangerous with the ball in his hands. He excelled against zone defenses at Clemson (though he's been slightly more efficient vs. man-to-man defense thus far in his rookie season).

Williams played less than half of the offensive snaps in each of Washington's first three games, but he's played about two-thirds of the offensive snaps in each of his last three games, and his role should continue to expand with McLaurin's season over.

There's appealing upside here, and it's possible Williams could start to earn enough targets every week to provide a sturdy PPR floor.

While Keon Coleman is the high-ceiling, low-floor waiver play among the Bills' WR corps, Khalil Shakir is the high-floor, low-ceiling option.

Shakir is averaging 5.3 targets a game but has had six or more targets in four of Buffalo's first six contests. The 26-year-old Shakir is averaging 3.7 catches and 48.3 receiving yards per game. He's scored only one touchdown in 2026 and has never had more than four TDs in a season.

Shakir has a solid matchup against the Ravens in Week 8. The Ravens play two-high safety coverage at the fifth-highest rate in the league, and Shakir is averaging a solid 0.47 PPR points per route run against two-high, according to Fantasy Points Data.

Jordyn Tyson is expected to play his first NFL game in Week 9 after the Saints come out of their bye. Tyson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury since mid-August.

The eighth overall pick in this year's draft, Tyson is a highly regarded prospect with few, if any, discernible weaknesses to his game. Durability has been an issue for Tyson, but his potential is immense.

This might be your last chance to get Tyson for a modest FAAB bid since the Saints are on bye this week. There are no guarantees Tyson will be able to stay healthy, but his top-10 draft pedigree speaks to the fantasy potential the young receiver has.

Over his last three games, Brenton Strange has 19-207-0 on 23 targets. Strange was TE7 in PPR scoring from Week 4 to Week 6 without scoring a touchdown.

With WR Brian Thomas Jr. having effectively vanished from the Jacksonville offense, Strange has been playing a larger role. Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence certainly doesn't mind throwing to tight ends. In 2023, Evan Engram had a 114-catch, 963-yard season while playing with Lawrence in Jacksonville.

Strange has thrived against single-high safety coverage shells this season, averaging 0.30 targets per route run and 2.82 yards per route run vs. single-high coverage. In Week 8, he faces a Colts defense that, entering Week 7, had played single-high safety at the 11th-highest rate in the league.

Third-round rookie Caleb Douglas returned from an ankle injury in Week 7 and had 2-70-2 on three targets, scoring on a 63-yard catch-and-run down the left sideline and running a nice in-breaking route to get open for a 7-yard TD catch in the back of the end zone.

Douglas was a standout in Miami's training camp, and he had 5-94-0 on seven targets in Week 1 before going down with the ankle injury in Week 2.

Yes, Douglas had only three targets on Sunday. Dolphins QB Malik Willis threw only 21 passes. Miami is low on passing volume most weeks, and that was certainly the case in Week 7.

But Douglas has been impressive. He could very well emerge as the Dolphins' No. 1 receiver this year. Douglas is a worthwhile upside play.

Christian McCaffrey left the 49ers' Week 7 game against the Falcons with a thigh injury before eventually returning. CMC's brief departure was a good reminder that rookie Kaelon Black might be the most indispensable handcuff RB in fantasy football. If McCaffrey were to miss time, Black would be ranked as a weekly RB1 in CMC's absence. Black led the 49ers with 12-63-1 rushing on Sunday. He and the 49ers are on bye this week, which should make Black easier to acquire.

Chig Okonkwo has had 60 or more receiving yards in two straight games, and he had a season-high seven catches on seven targets when we last saw the Commanders in their Week 6 loss to the 49ers.

Okonkwo figures to be an important part of the Commanders' passing game now that Washington's top wide receiver, Terry McLaurin, will miss the rest of the season with a torn patellar tendon.

Although he's never had more than 560 receiving yards or three touchdowns in a season since entering the league in 2022, Okonkwo could be poised for his best year to date. He's averaging a career-high 37.5 receiving yards per game and 7.5 yards per target. With good health, Okonkwo could shatter his previous single-season high of 79 targets.

Okonkwo is a solid Week 8 TE option even against an Eagles defense that has allowed the 11th-fewest fantasy points per game to TEs.

Ashton Jeanty is in a rushing slump. The sixth overall pick of the 2025 draft is averaging 3.1 yards per carry this season and 2.3 yards per carry over his last three games. Jeanty has rushed for fewer than 30 yards in three consecutive games.

Rookie Mike Washington Jr. is averaging 4.9 yards per carry. Entering Week 7, he had averaged an impressive 2.74 yards after contact per attempt, per Fantasy Points Data.

Washington has been a more effective runner than Jeanty. But because Jeanty has been so dynamic as a pass catcher, he's not a candidate for demotion. He could, however, lose early-down carries to Washington.

With the possibility of a boost in rushing attempts that could lead to stand-alone value, Washington is more than just a handcuff.

There has been speculation that the stumbling Colts could hold a fire sale and potentially trade star RB Jonathan Taylor. That possibility might make the Colts' No. 2 running back, rookie Seth McGowan, worth a speculative add. McGowan had season highs in carries (11) and rushing yards (46) Sunday against the Vikings.

If rookie Jeremiyah Love returns from his ankle injury this week, Bam Knight will have virtually zero fantasy value. But if Love misses a third straight game, Knight could offer flex value at the very least in Week 8.

Knight had 15-80-0 rushing against the Rams in Week 6 and added 2-18-0 receiving. In Week 7, Knight had 7-48-0 rushing and 3-15-0 receiving vs. the Broncos.

Knight has been splitting snaps and touches pretty evenly with Tyler Allgeier while Love has been out, but Knight has been a more effective runner than Allgeier the last two weeks. A near-50/50 share of touches could translate into decent Week 8 fantasy value against a Dallas run defense that ranks 25th in defense-adjusted value over average (DVOA) and 23rd in expected points added per rush.

But again, Love's return could nuke Knight's fantasy value, so do your due diligence on Love's status before bidding on Bam.

In his first two games back from the wrist injury he sustained in Week 1, promising rookie Ja'Kobi Lane has had 7-65-0 on 10 targets.

Lane, who drew rave reviews in training camp, is an interesting speculative add with Ravens QB Lamar Jackson likely to be back from an ankle injury this week.

After getting one more carry than Chase Brown in the Bengals' Week 5 win over the Dolphins, Samaje Perine was out-carried by Brown 11-4 in a Week 7 win over the Ravens — although Perine did punch in a late touchdown in that game. There is no longer any pretense of stand-alone value for Perine, but Brown stakeholders might want to consider adding Perine as a handcuff at some point.

Keon Coleman has scored a touchdown in three consecutive games, averaging 12.1 yards per target and 2.53 yards per route run over that span, with a 17.6% target share.

Coleman has been playing an expanded role for the Bills in recent weeks with WR DJ Moore dealing with a shoulder injury. Moore has played only one of the Bills' last three games and was limited to 23 snaps in the one game he played over that stretch. Coleman has played at least 70% of Buffalo's offensive snaps in his last three games, culminating in a season-high 85.3% snap share against the Raiders in Week 6 before the Bills went on bye.

He hasn't had more than seven targets in any game this season, but Coleman has been making some serious hay with his targets, and it's possible he's turned a corner after two pretty rough seasons to begin his NFL career.

With Moore potentially back in Week 8, Coleman's target outlook is going to be murky. Still, based on his recent performances, Coleman might be a worthwhile dart throw.

Jets TE Mason Taylor had his finest game of the season Sunday against the Dolphins, with 5-62-2 on six targets. Taylor led the Jets' tight ends in snaps and routes run on Sunday, with rookie first-rounder Kenyon Sadiq playing a limited role. Taylor had one touchdown in 17 previous NFL games, and he hadn't had more than 33 receiving yards in a game before Week 7. Taylor's usage is increasing, so he's worth keeping on the radar, but he isn't worth rostering yet.

Terrance Ferguson remains on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain, but he's eligible to return and could be back as early as this week.

With Davante Adams expected to miss about two months with a major hamstring injury, tight ends are going to play an outsized role in the Rams' offense for the foreseeable future.

In Week 7, Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen combined for 11-82-2 on 14 targets. Ferguson is younger and far more athletic than any of those three.

Ferguson had 6-54-1 on nine targets against the Broncos in Week 2 and appeared to be on the verge of a breakout. Then he got hurt in Week 3, and he's been out ever since.

If Ferguson is still available in your league and you're unhappy with your TE situation, you owe it to yourself to try to acquire him.

After scoring two touchdowns against the Raiders in Week 5 and another TD against the Jets in Week 6, DeMario Douglas was quiet against the Bears in Week 7, with 3-23-0 on four targets on a night when Patriots QB Drake Maye threw for 321 yards.

A.J. Brown has returned from his ankle injury and is the clear No. 1 receiver for New England, even though he hasn't played well in his first two games back. Beyond Brown, the Patriots get inconsistent contributions from an ensemble cast of pass catchers.

Douglas played 65% of the Patriots' offensive snaps in Week 7. He played one more snap than WR Efton Chism. Kyle Williams played 21 snaps. Patriots TEs Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon combined for 10-127-1 on 11 targets. WRs Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs are both on IR but are likely to return in November.

It's hard to see Douglas providing long-term value, but he could be a useful pinch hitter this week in deeper leagues courtesy of a matchup with the Dolphins, who have one of the worst secondaries in the league.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. doesn't catch passes and has little if any stand-alone value as the Jaguars' No. 2 running back behind Bhayshul Tuten, who has convincingly seized the lead role in the Jacksonville backfield. But Rodriguez is a compelling handcuff as the clear No. 2 in a good offense.

It seemed as if Tyler Higbee was poised for a big game against the Raiders in Week 7. He had 22-234-1 in his previous four games, and the absence of WR Davante Adams figured to keep the targets coming.

But Higbee took a backseat to two of the Rams' other tight ends on Sunday. Colby Parkinson had 5-48-0. Davis Allen had 4-20-2, scoring the Rams' first two touchdowns in a 35-21 win. Higbee had 2-14-0 on three targets.

It was a disappointing performance, but Higbee led the Rams' TEs in routes and is still the best bet among this group for Week 8. That is, unless Terrance Ferguson comes off injured reserve this week.

But even if Ferguson is back and Higbee is merely the second-best bet among the Rams' tight ends, Higbee could still be in play as a streaming tight end for Week 8.

Sunday was National Tight Ends Day, and the Dolphins' Greg Dulcich celebrated with his best game of the season to date, finishing with 5-86-0 on five targets. We wouldn't recommend chasing the breakout game. Dulcich has averaged 3.7 targets this season in one of the NFL's least potent passing attacks and is still looking for his first touchdown of the season.

Chris Bell was third among Miami's receivers in snaps and routes in the Dolphins' Week 7 win over the Jets, trailing Malik Washington and fellow rookie Caleb Douglas in those categories. The Dolphins' low-volume passing attack isn't going to accommodate a No. 3 receiver for fantasy purposes. But Bell is an intriguing talent with an appealing combination of size (6-2, 228) and speed. He's worth stashing if you have a roster spot to spare.
